newsitem.title: USA: Lawmaker says EPA of suppressed air rule comments.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker says EPA of suppressed air rule comments.

text.p: The chairman of the House Commerce Committee said Wednesday the Environmental Protection Agency suppressed comments from the administration which the EPA said could damage its effort to set stricter air quality standards.

Virginia Republican Thomas Bliley said he was "seriously concerned that the EPA may be exerting extraordinary control" over an Office of Management and Budget that drafted a response to Bliley's queries on the OMB review of the proposed air standards.

At a news conference, he released a copy of an EPA memo that said the OMB draft response could be "very damaging" to the administration's controversial proposal to tighten air standards against soot and smog.
Bliley and other Republicans so far have given a cool reception to the proposal that industry groups say would cost billions of dollars to implement.

The EPA memo "strongly recommended" that the OMB use language more similar to language used by the EPA in its response to Bliley's queries, and said the OMB draft did not accurately reflect how the administration reviewed the proposal.
Bliley demanded the original draft of the OMB response, and accused the EPA of "an apparent lack of forthrightness in dealing with this committee."
But a spokesman from the OMB said the exchange with the EPA was routine and did not compromise the OMB's independence.

"Draft correspondence at OMB moves up a certain food chain ... and goes through layers of review to ensure accuracy, not only factual accuracy but accuracy with regard to presidential policy," Lawrence Haas, OMB associate communications director, said.
